note: Entry point: attacker-controlled input buffer of 3 bytes ('''') is passed to the config parser
Lexer initialized: pos points to start of input, end points to data+3 (end of buffer)
First single-quote consumed; lexer->pos points to remaining "''". The strncmp confirms multiline string start, so lex_multiline_string is called
peek() reads the 2nd quote (returns '\''), so end = "'''" (the closing delimiter to search for)
advance_n(2) skips past the 2nd and 3rd quotes. lexer->pos now equals lexer->end (end of buffer)
OUT-OF-BOUNDS READ: strncmp reads 3 bytes starting at lexer->end, which is past the allocated buffer. This triggers the global-buffer-overflow READ 1 ASAN crash
Root cause: advance_n moves pos to end-of-buffer, but the loop unconditionally dereferences pos via strncmp before checking for EOF via next()
